jobs.title: Supply Chain Program Manager
jobs.description:
WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy.

As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in.

We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide.

This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today.

We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level.

Join us and let’s shape the future of data.

Job Description

As a Supply Chain Program Manager in the Supply Chain Center of Excellence, you will work alongside some of the most experienced and accomplished minds across Western Digital's Supply Chain functions, while engaging with the newest and most cutting-edge ideas in the field. Your role is to bring the two together, combining proven expertise with emerging thinking so that they work in harmony and deliver results.

You will be awarded opportunities across the full spectrum of Supply Chain functions, engaging with established leaders in Logistics, Direct Procurement, Indirect Procurement, Planning, Risk and Resiliency, Operations and beyond. Rather than relying on authority, you will build consensus through influence and persuasion, grounded in both hard facts and qualitative insight. Success depends on strong dependency management, stakeholder alignment and clear communication across functions that may have other priorities.

How we Operate

These are the behaviors expected every day. They map to the WD Leadership Expectations and define the standard that this position role models for the wider team.

Own the outcome, not the tracker. The plan is an instrument. The measure is whether the ramp landed on time, at cost and at quality.
Champion clear decisions. Most Program delay is undecided, not unknown. Frame the choice, name the decider, get it made and record it.
Manage the seams. Functions are usually competent inside their own boundary. Programs fail between them, which is where the Program Manager works.
Escalate early with a recommendation. Raise it when there is still room to act, and bring the option you would choose.
Be direct and transparent about status. Green that turns red without warning destroys credibility permanently. Report what is, not what is hoped.
Influence without direct line authority. Nobody on the Program reports to you. Credibility, preparation and reliability are the only levers — build them deliberately.
Close the loop. A Program that ends without lessons captured has spent the organization’s learning and kept none of it

Key Responsibilities

Strong Program Management Skills

Integrated planning and governance. Own the master plan, milestones, dependencies, owners, RAID log and steering committee cadence across all workstreams, with an independent view of status.
Scope, schedule and budget control. Protect the baseline, manage change through a disciplined process, and keep the program on time and on budget.
Risk and decision management. Surface risks early, frame decisions with options and a recommendation, and record outcomes so they are not relitigated.
Run the Program cadence at the right rhythm for the phase
Maintain a single source of truth for Program status
Define and enforce entry and exit criteria at each gate

Program Portfolio Leadership and Team Development

Own a portfolio of supply chain Programs, including major ramps and transitions of high complexity
Lead, coach and develop the Program Managers running them, building advanced proficiency across the Program management toolkit
Set the Program management standard for the function: plans, cadence, gates, reporting and post-Program review
Frame executive decisions, manage complex risk and drive cross-functional alignment without authority

Stakeholder Alignment

Cross-functional alignment. Bring together Legal, Direct Materials, Indirect Procurement, Logistics, Sales, Finance and IT, each with different contract types, risk tolerances and priorities.
Balancing competing priorities. Reconcile Legal’s risk posture, Procurement’s efficiency goals and the business’s need for speed into decisions all parties can support.
Composure with difficult stakeholders. Remain calm, respectful and fact-based when challenged; depersonalize conflict and keep the focus on outcomes.
Earned trust and sponsorship. Involve skeptics early, give them a real voice in design, and use executive sponsors and escalation paths deliberately.

Cross-Functional Dependency Management

Map dependencies across Sourcing, Engineering, Quality, Operations, Planning and suppliers
Track dependency status and drive owners to their commitments
Resolve cross-functional conflicts at the working level where possible
Escalate blocked dependencies with the decision required clearly stated

Risk and Decision Management

Maintain a live Program risk register with owners, mitigations and trigger points
Run scenario analysis on the risks that could move the Program
Frame decisions clearly: the choice, the options, the trade-offs, the recommendation, the decider
Track decisions and their rationale so they are not relitigated

Delivery and Adoption Discipline

Fit to standard. Champion out-of-the-box capability and challenge customization that adds cost and risk without clear value.
Testing and cutover. Lead system integration and user acceptance testing, data migration validation and a well-rehearsed go-live.
Adoption and value. Drive training, change champions and adoption metrics such as contract cycle time, and confirm the business case is realized.
Measure adoption and sustainment, and reinforce new behaviors until they become the way Western Digital works

Change management

Lead organizational change that turns new processes, tools and ways of working into lasting habits across the enterprise
Build a compelling case for change and inspire stakeholders at every level, from executive sponsors to frontline teams
Design adoption roadmaps with clear communication, training and engagement plans that bring people along, not just systems
Identify and empower change champions who carry new practices into their own functions and regions
Anticipate resistance early and turn skeptics into advocates through listening, evidence and quick wins

Executive Communication and Decision Framing

Report Program status honestly, concisely and consistently
Frame executive decisions with the choice, options, trade-offs and a recommendation
Run executive forums that produce decisions rather than updates
Manage expectations early rather than explaining misses afterwards
Executive communication. Deliver concise, candid status that lets sponsors act quickly and with confidence.
Governance. Run a structured governance process to include daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly core team and steering Committee meetings
Collateral development. Create update templates and work individually and with team members to create executive communication collateral

Program Analytics and Reporting

Build and maintain readiness and status dashboards
Use data rather than narrative to drive Program conversations
Track leading indicators, not just milestone completion
Adopt tooling, automation, and AI that reduce reporting effort

Post-Program Learning

Run honest post-Program reviews covering what worked and what did not
Convert lessons into process change with the relevant process owner
Share learning across the Program community
Improve templates, gates and standards based on what was learned

Business Process Transformation

Champion innovation by challenging how work is done today and envisioning how it should be done tomorrow
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and digitize end-to-end business processes across supply chain functions
Oversee transformation projects from concept through delivery, ensuring they meet scope, schedule and value commitments
Partner with IT and business owners to align process redesign with enabling systems, data and AI capabilities
Measure the impact of each transformation and feed the lessons into the next wave of improvement

What would success look like

Big bets that land. Bold programs and transformations delivered on time, on budget and at the quality customers expect.
Problems solved before they surface. Risks and gaps spotted early and closed well ahead of the moment they could hurt the business.
A supply chain ready for what's next. Capacity, capability and technology in place before demand arrives, not after.
Change without chaos. New processes, tools and transitions rolled out smoothly, with no disruption to customers and no value left on the table.
A voice leaders trust. Reporting so candid and reliable that there are never surprises, and status always reflects reality.
Decisions made in the room. Choices framed so clearly that leaders can act on the spot and keep momentum high.
A legacy that compounds. Every lesson turned into a lasting standard, so each program makes the next one faster, smarter and better.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Engineering, Business or a related field
10+ years of experience in supply chain, operations or program management, including leading product ramps, technology transitions or supplier readiness in a high-tech, semiconductor or electronics manufacturing environment
A track record of leading process improvement or transformation work with measurable results
Hands-on familiarity with AI and automation, including generative AI tools, and the curiosity to apply them to real supply chain problems
Organizational change management experience
Experience leading and developing Program Managers or cross-functional teams
Demonstrated ability to frame executive decisions and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority
Strong working knowledge of supplier capacity, qualification, engineering change and end-of-life management
Proficiency with program analytics and dashboarding tools

Preferred

Experience in data storage or hard disk drive supply chains
Delivering AI and machine learning use cases, such as predictive supplier risk, demand sensing and generative AI assistants
Experience with control towers, digital twins and supplier risk platforms
Setting up or maturing a Program Management Office, which ties to the next-generation PMO in the opening
Leading scenario planning, tabletop exercises or business continuity programs
A background in consulting, transformation offices or a center of excellence
Familiarity with sustainability, ESG and trade-compliance requirements
Working with global teams and Asia-based supplier networks
Change management certification (e.g., Prosci) or a record of leading large-scale adoption programs

Programs are where every part of the supply chain organization has to work as one. This role holds limited authority and all of the accountability, which makes credibility the entire currency of the role. Earn it by being prepared, being honest about status, and forcing the decisions nobody else wants to call.

In summary, the Program Manager is encouraged to bring innovation and creativity to every challenge, and fresh thinking about where the supply chain should go next will always be welcome. You will not be starting from a blank page: Western Digital is already pursuing a number of cutting-edge initiatives, and you will have the opportunity to shape, accelerate and expand them.

LINK is a fast-growing Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) that leverages human-centered design to support strategy, innovation, communication, change, and branding within the federal government and adjacent industry partners. At LINK, we partner with engineers, futurists, and thought leaders to untangle complexity, discover opportunity, and communicate clearly with visual stories.

Let us be your partners in change.

Location:
We are actively hiring in the San Diego area.

About The Opportunity

LINK is actively seeking a Senior Strategist; Program Manager
to join our dynamic team, where we leverage strong partnerships and a robust portfolio of clients across diverse industries. You will be responsible for leading and executing innovative design strategies, collaborating with both internal teams and executive-level clients, and driving impactful visual storytelling to meet client objectives.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced professional to bring a combination of creative and strategic expertise to elevate LINK’s business growth and deliver high-quality, human-centered design solutions. You will work closely with clients to understand their challenges, develop compelling narratives, and implement design strategies that align with their mission, goals, and brand identity. Ideal candidates will have a proven track record of designing impactful visual experiences, utilizing data-driven insights, and collaborating cross-functionally to deliver exceptional client results.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communication, English, Business, or a related field
10+ years of experience in strategic communication, public affairs, program management, or strategy development
7+ years program/project management experience including familiarity with Agile methodologies and project delivery best practices
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, maintaining a strong focus on accuracy and attention to detail
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate in a clear, approachable, and knowledgeable manner
Government contracting experience
PMP certification preferred
Experience with human-centered design and design thinking principles
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously

Responsibilities

Senior Strategist responsibilities include:

Client Partnership & Design Strategy Leadership

Serves as a trusted advisor to clients by framing complex challenges, identifying opportunities, and applying human-centered design approaches to inform strategic decision-making.
Partners directly with client stakeholders to understand organizational priorities, user needs, operational constraints, and desired outcomes.
Leads the development of design strategy approaches that align stakeholder needs, business objectives, and mission requirements.
Guides cross-functional teams through ambiguity, helping stakeholders build alignment and make informed decisions.
Identifies opportunities to create tangible business value and support long-term client success.
Provides guidance that helps clients make informed decisions and navigate organizational complexity.

Content Strategy, Storytelling & Execution

Translates complex ideas into compelling strategic narratives, executive-level presentations, communication strategies, and decision-support products.
Develops messaging frameworks that align leadership vision, organizational priorities, and stakeholder needs.
Define content structures, information hierarchies, and storytelling approaches that communicate complex concepts clearly and effectively.
Collaborates with creative teams to develop high-quality visual products that support strategic objectives and audience understanding.
Establishes quality standards for strategic deliverables and provides guidance to team members to ensure consistency and excellence.
Leads development of executive-ready materials that support decision-making, alignment, and organizational action.

Change Management & Organizational Transformation

Develops and implements change management strategies, including stakeholder engagement plans, communications strategies, change impact assessments, and adoption roadmaps.
Designs governance frameworks, operating models, and implementation approaches that support successful transformation efforts.
Facilitates cross-functional working sessions that drive alignment, accelerate decision-making, and address organizational resistance.
Establishes feedback mechanisms and performance measures that support continuous improvement and long-term success.
Monitors progress, evaluates outcomes, and refines approaches based on stakeholder feedback and organizational needs.

Research, Insight Development & Systems Thinking

Leads mixed-method research efforts, including stakeholder interviews, contextual inquiry, observations, journey mapping, ecosystem analysis, and systems mapping activities.
Synthesizes qualitative and quantitative findings into actionable insights, opportunity areas, strategic recommendations, and design directions.
Applies systems thinking to identify patterns, dependencies, root causes, and opportunities across complex organizational environments.
Translates technical, operational, and policy-focused challenges into human-centered insights and strategic considerations.
Guides research activities that inform organizational transformation, service design, experience design, and strategic planning efforts.

Develops facilitation approaches, agendas, exercises, and collaborative experiences that enable productive dialogue and structured problem-solving.
Synthesizes workshop outputs into actionable findings, recommendations, and implementation considerations.
Helps stakeholders navigate competing priorities, organizational complexity, and change initiatives through structured facilitation and engagement.
Guides teams in applying human-centered design methods throughout project lifecycles.

Team Development & Leadership

Mentors teammates through coaching, knowledge sharing, and constructive feedback.
Models LINK values and contributes to a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture.
Shares tools, approaches, and lessons learned that improve the quality and consistency of work across engagements.

Maintain strong client relationships and serve as a trusted advisor to client stakeholders.
Collaborate with clients to understand challenges, define priorities, manage expectations, and identify opportunities to create additional value.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Software
jobs.description:
About Mind:

Mind Robotics is building Physical AI for real-world industrial deployment, starting with the factory floor. We believe the hardest problems in AI are solved when researchers and engineers are hands-on with the physical world every day - and we're looking for people who are passionate about robotics, value ownership, and are excited to tackle difficult problems. Join us if you want to move beyond digital intelligence and put intelligence into motion.

About the team and the role:

Program Management at Mind is an operational catalyst. We own outcomes, drive the trade-offs that keep engineering moving, and set the metabolic rate of the teams we partner with — clearing roadblocks, closing stalled decisions, carrying risk upward, and protecting the focus engineers need to build. As a Software Program Manager you will own the integrated program plan across all of software and build the practice itself: how teams define their own milestones and commit to org-level ones, how we know week over week whether we are on or off track, and how problems surface early enough that we can still do something about them. You will partner directly with hardware program management so that software and hardware roll up into one program picture rather than two competing ones.

Responsibilities:

End-to-End Ownership: Own the software program plan end to end — from roadmap planning through implementation, integration, validation, and release to the fleet — and own the functional outcome, not just the schedule.
Program Practice Design: Establish how software program management works at Mind: the planning rhythm that connects team-level work to org-level milestones, what qualifies as a milestone, what "done" means at each one, and the artifacts that support both the individual engineer and leadership in prioritization and decision making.
Milestone Planning: Build software plans that align with org-level milestones, including clear definitions of what “done” means at each step.
Metric Tracking: Monitor and report on key program metrics, and communicate status, blockers, and risks to leadership.
Progress Tracking & Status Integrity: Build the tracking layer that answers whether we are on or off track, drawn from the systems teams already work in.
Risk Mitigation: Identify and escalate technical, dependency, and resourcing risks early, and and drive them to resolution.
Technical / Business Judgment: Engage directly in architecture and design discussions at a depth sufficient to stress-test engineering estimates and pressure-test readiness. Drive decisions at that level with understanding of the impacts to our business goals.

Requirements:

Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in engineering (software / computer science preferred), or equivalent experience.
Industry Experience: 5+ years of experience in technical program management for software products, ideally in robotics, autonomous systems, or another domain where software ships against hardware and real-world deployment constraints.
Proven Track Record: Demonstrated success taking software from early development through release and sustained operation.
Technical Depth: Strong software fundamentals with the ability to engage meaningfully in architecture, planning, and systems integration discussions.
System Complexity: Experience managing programs spanning multiple interdependent software domains along with their dependencies on hardware revisions and the availability of test hardware.
Execution & Ownership: High sense of urgency, comfortable with ambiguity, and driven by an "engineering curiosity" to understand how the entire system works.

Travel is expected approximately 10-20% domestically and internationally to support manufacturing site engagements and deployment activities.

The Engineering Program Manager leads multiple complex engineering programs within the Imaging portfolio, translating portfolio strategy into executable program plans and driving delivery of machine vision technologies across global manufacturing environments. You'll turn data requirements into capture programs that work across devices, operators, and locations. Clear written communication, including operating procedures, technical decisions, and realistic delivery forecasts.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager, ERP Transformation
jobs.description:
The Sr. Project Manager, ERP Transformation
is responsible for leading Trinidad Benham's enterprise-wide ERP transformation program, overseeing the rollout of a custom-built ERP platform across 20+ facilities and business functions, including accounting/finance as well as operations. This role serves as the single point of accountability for program delivery across both business and Information Technology teams, driving execution, governance, stakeholder alignment, organizational change, and measurable operational improvements. Working closely with executive leadership, including the CEO and CIO, this position influences strategic decisions, manages competing priorities, and ensures the successful delivery and adoption of solutions that support the company's long-term business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Program Ownership and Pace

Own the integrated program plan end to end, building it where one does not yet exist, covering scope, schedule, milestones, dependencies, and resources across every workstream, including requirements, development, data migration, integrations, reporting, testing, and cutover.
Set and defend the facility rollout cadence, and be accountable for increasing it as the program matures.
Drive every contributing team, business and IT alike, to committed dates, and escalate immediately and at the appropriate level of leadership when a commitment is at risk.
Maintain the program decision, risk, issue, and action lists with a named owner, a due date, and a current status on every open item, and personally chase items to closure.
Present executive leadership with a single, unvarnished view of commitments and status across all teams, including when a delay originates inside Information Technology.
Hold third-party vendors and implementation partners accountable to their committed deliverables and dates on the same basis as internal teams.

Business Outcomes and Value Realization

Be accountable for the operational outcomes each release and each facility go-live is intended to deliver, not only for the go-live itself.
Work with business owners to define measurable outcomes before work begins, such as order cycle time, inventory accuracy, financial close duration, on-time shipment, or labor per unit, and report achievement against them after each go-live.
Challenge scope that does not create measurable business value, and press for the smallest release that delivers it, so working capability reaches users sooner and improves through iteration.
Drive process improvement rather than process replication. Where the business asks to reproduce a legacy process in the new platform, surface it and bring the decision to the business owner and the steering committee.
Ensure trade-offs between scope, date, and cost are made deliberately by the business, with downstream implications made explicit, rather than absorbed by default into the schedule.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Governance

Serve as the single accountable owner of the program across Production, Warehouse Management, Accounting and Finance, Customer Service, Traffic, and Procurement, and across Business Applications, Software Engineering, Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity. One owner spanning business and IT, not one on each side.
Establish and operate program governance, including an executive steering committee attended by the Chief Executive Officer and the functional executive leadership team, and maintain the risk and issue registers behind it.
Prepare and personally present program status, decisions, and recommendations to the CEO and the executive leadership team, and produce material supporting Board-level reporting.
Propose prioritization across product teams, confirm it with the functional leads, and escalate where agreement cannot be reached rather than absorbing the conflict into the plan.
Hold business areas and Information Technology equally to agreed commitments on subject matter expert availability, testing windows, and decision turnaround.
Serve as the point of contact that reduces the coordination burden carried by business leaders, escalating into IT on their behalf when they are blocked.
Bridge communication between executive sponsors, business owners, end users, and the product, design, architecture, and development teams, ensuring each has what it needs from the others.

Sequencing, Scope, and Change Control

Build and maintain one schedule that reconciles two-week sprint cadence, the monthly and annual financial close calendar, fixed facility go-live dates, and plant operating and seasonal constraints.
Establish the sequence and phasing of roadmap delivery in coordination with Product Management and Product Ownership.
Hold requirements stable once a release is committed, and assess every proposed change for impact on schedule, resourcing, and dependent workstreams before it is accepted.
Ensure financial reporting requirements are defined, agreed, and held stable early in each release, given their dependence on the underlying data model and their sensitivity to late change.
Identify where program work conflicts with business operating constraints and raise it early enough to be addressed.

Delivery, Testing, and Go-Live Readiness

Own program go-live dates, define the readiness criteria that govern each facility go-live, and obtain formal sign-off from each business owner at every gate.
Plan testing windows jointly with business areas and track progress through functional testing, User Acceptance Testing, and deployment activities.
Track defect resolution through to closure ahead of each release.
Carry each facility from planning through cutover, go-live, stabilization, and transition to production support.

Compliance and Controls

Capture regulatory, audit, food safety, traceability, and internal control requirements as program requirements at the start of each release, rather than allowing them to surface late in testing.
Coordinate with Accounting and Finance leadership to confirm that delivered functionality adheres to applicable standards, including GAAP and internal audit controls, and that those requirements are validated prior to each facility go-live.

Adoption and Organizational Readiness

Own change management and adoption planning across affected business areas, raising gaps and conflicts to leadership for resolution.
Monitor delivery of role-based training through each department training lead, and raise gaps where staff will not be ready to operate the new system at go-live.
Track organizational readiness by business area, identifying sources of resistance and other adoption barriers early enough to be addressed before go-live.
Convene all affected business areas when new capability or significant change is introduced, so requirements are captured before design rather than after.

Continuous Improvement

Identify and implement opportunities to improve program predictability, delivery speed, and stakeholder satisfaction.
Apply AI tools to improve project management, program reporting, and delivery execution.

Perform other duties as assigned by management.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

Required Experience

Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive project or program management experience leading enterprise application initiatives.
Experience leading at least one full lifecycle ERP or enterprise system implementation through production go-live.
Demonstrated experience delivering custom-developed software solutions.
Proven experience leading business transformation initiatives that resulted in measurable operational improvements.
Experience managing complex, cross-functional programs involving multiple workstreams, business functions, and integrated systems.
Experience operating within regulated or controlled environments where financial, regulatory, audit, or compliance requirements influence solution design and delivery.
Experience working directly with executive leadership teams to facilitate decisions, communicate program status, and drive organizational alignment.
Experience utilizing AI-enabled tools to improve project management, business analysis, testing, or delivery processes.

Preferred education and experience

Experience supporting manufacturing, distribution, food production, or comparable operating environments.
Experience leading or supporting a financial ERP implementation, including general ledger structure, accounts payable and receivable, asset management, and financial close.
Familiarity with the control and compliance environment surrounding financial systems, including GAAP and internal audit controls.
Experience with multi-site or phased rollouts across distributed operations.

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or equivalent demonstrated experience.
PgMP, PMI-ACP, Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), SAFe, or similar certifications.
Experience with Azure DevOps, Notion, Jira, or similar Agile planning and portfolio management tools.

jobs.title: Security-Compliance Program Manager
jobs.description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role

We are looking for a Security-Compliance Program Manager to join our team. This is a Remote role, reporting to the Director, Global Security-Compliance Practice in the Global Security Compliance department. Compliance helps Zscaler win. When a Zscaler team member, a customer, or a partner hits a compliance requirement, our practice is who they call trust to answer. You'll be one of the people behind building trust: part advisor, part translator, part teacher. You'll help customers navigate compliance frameworks like Zero Trust, GDPR, NIST, PCI, and HIPAA, and you'll help our field teams turn compliance requirements into relevant, relevant, and winning conversations. In every room you walk into, you'll live at the intersection of security, data protection, and compliance, making the case for how Zscaler protects customers and their data in a compliant way. This is not a back-office audit job. You'll be in front of customers, in deals, and on stage.

What you’ll do (Role Expectations)

Represent the practice directly with customers through calls, webinars, and conferences, while clearly communicating how compliance helps accelerate deals instead of slowing them down
Map compliance frameworks to Zscaler capabilities control by control, using published methodology and clear labels for what we meet, partially meet, support, or leave to the customer
Build reusable playbooks and assets from deal-based learnings so the broader field can respond faster and more consistently next time
Educate SEs and AEs to handle routine compliance conversations themselves, while keeping data security at the center of every discussion so requirements stay tied to protecting customer data
Act as a security-compliance first responder, completing vendor security questionnaires and customer assessments accurately, quickly, and without overclaiming, while assembling the evidence and documentation needed to support responses

Who You Are (Success Profile)

You operate with a strong sense of ownership and a passion for the mission, seamlessly navigating between high-level strategy and hands-on execution to deliver high-quality outcomes.
You are a high-trust partner who thrives on collaborative feedback, matching ambition for the team with direct, respectful communication to build trust.
You are a pragmatic builder who enjoys rolling up your sleeves to create and iterate, balancing technical execution with the rapid delivery of value.
You bring clarity to complex situations, outstandingly distilling technical and compliance concepts into simple, actionable plans and communication.
You maintain composure in fast-paced environments, viewing setbacks as opportunities and guiding team members through complexity with adaptability and resilience.

What We’re Looking For (Minimum Qualifications)

Foundational understanding of AI/ML technologies and experience leveraging, securing, or positioning AI-driven solutions to optimize outcomes within your functional domain
Zscaler product understanding or the ability to build it fast, enabling you to know what the platform actually does before saying what it satisfies
Global compliance fluency, including working knowledge of major frameworks (such as NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, ISO 27001, DORA, GDPR, or regional equivalents) and the ability to pick up new ones quickly
Comprehensive understanding of security, data security, and compliance, including how security architecture works, how data is protected in motion and at rest, and how compliance frameworks formalize both
The ability to translate perspectives: technology to compliance, compliance to business, and business to sales
Field credibility with experience working with or in sales or customer-facing teams, and a bias to execute to deliver good answers quickly instead of waiting for perfection

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

Proven ability to leverage AI technologies and workflows to drive measurable operational efficiency
Compliance or security certifications (CISSP, CCSP, ISO 27001 LA, CCP, CCA, or similar)
Experience in federal, SLED, healthcare, or other regulated industries, with eligibility for a US security clearance being a plus
Experience presenting at industry events or building enablement content

The CSM is responsible for the leadership development of the people that report to them, while also accountable for security operations delivery at these datacenters. The CSM partners with Security and Datacenter Operations senior leadership and management teams to help drive operational effectiveness, superior performance, and audit readiness. Responsible for preserving an environment where people and property are safe and well-protected, the CSM utilizes their professional experience to manage people with varying skillsets and develop effective strategies to drive improvement. The CSM reports directly to the regional security manager, and works alongside other site security managers in their metro

What you’ll do

In this role, you will lead and manage physical security operations across multiple critical infrastructure facilities, ensuring a safe, consistent, and effective security program. You will actively manage and develop site security personnel by partnering with local branch leadership to support recruiting, hiring, onboarding, training, coaching, and performance management, while ensuring all team members are treated with dignity and respect. You will drive safety as a core operational priority, implementing safety programs and initiatives with the goal of zero workplace injuries.

You will plan, assign, and oversee physical security projects and daily operational tasks, evaluating the effectiveness of site security programs and recommending improvements where needed. You will set the standard for strong customer service and professional communication, holding site teams accountable to the same expectations. In partnership with the Regional Security Manager, you will monitor site health and key performance indicators, support unannounced audits, and strengthen overall team performance.

Additionally, you will engage regularly with clients and Securitas leadership through account reviews, security planning, assessments, and ongoing communication, ensuring leadership is informed of key accomplishments, risks, and concerns. You will build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders and split time across assigned sites to maintain operational awareness, lead teams effectively, and continuously develop and enhance the physical security program.

What you need to apply

To apply for this role, you should have at least four years of experience in the security industry, including four years in a management role, along with an associate degree in Security Management, Business Management, or a related field. Proficiency with Microsoft Office is required, and experience working in a datacenter environment is a plus. Preferred qualifications include working knowledge of security technologies such as CCTV, access control systems, incident management platforms, and video surveillance software, as well as a bachelor's degree in criminal justice, Security Management, Business Management, or a related discipline. Professional security certifications such as CPP or PSP are also preferred.

This position involves travel (approximately 10% of the time), so a passion for travel (and a valid passport) is essential. This role may also have to work nights and weekends to support high priority events and off-hours incidents. All applicants to this role must have reliable means of communication, reliable means of transportation (public or private) to get to/from work, the legal right to work in the country where the position is located, and the ability to speak, read and write in English proficiently.

What you’ll get

We offer more than just a job; we offer the chance to be part of a collaborative and supportive team where your contributions are valued and your growth matters. In this role, you will thrive in a dynamic environment while supporting a prestigious multinational client account. You will gain exposure to global operations and cross-regional collaboration, and you will have access to continuous learning, training programs, and career development opportunities designed to help you succeed.

The extra stuff

This position requires—with or without reasonable accommodation—the physical and mental ability to perform all essential job functions effectively. This includes maintaining composure under pressure while interacting with clients, authorities, executives, and staff; working independently without direct supervision; and managing multiple tasks simultaneously. The role involves regular use of a computer and a keyboard. Visual acuity for both near and far distances, as well as the ability to adjust focus, is required. The position may involve handling sensitive or confidential information and requires flexibility in scheduling to meet operational demands.

This standardized global job description is intended to define the core responsibilities and requirements of the Campus Security Manager role across regions. Local addenda may be applied to address country-specific legal, regulatory, language, or clearance requirements without altering the core role definition.

jobs.description:
🌟 Who We Are Looking For

Good with Macs, serious about security and keen to build something great? We are looking for an IT & Security Manager
to take ownership of CorePlan’s internal IT and security foundations as we grow globally.

CorePlan is a Perth-born SaaS company shaking up the mining industry with our digital drilling management platform. We replace paper and spreadsheets with connected workflows used by customers around the world.

You will help our crew work securely and effectively, keeping everyday IT running smoothly while strengthening our security and compliance program.

Reporting to the CFO
on compliance, budget and risk, and working closely with our CTO
on technical architecture and cloud security, you will combine hands-on problem-solving with bigger-picture thinking.

There is plenty to own and plenty of room to make your mark.

🛠 What Will You Do?

Keep our crew connected: Manage our predominantly Mac device fleet, support employees and improve self-service guidance.
Own identity and access: Administer Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, including MFA, conditional access, licences and access reviews.
Strengthen our defences: Implement and monitor security controls, logging and alerts across our internal IT and AWS environments.
Keep compliance moving: Support SOC 2 and ISO 27001 requirements, maintain documentation and coordinate penetration testing.
Be ready when it counts: Lead incident response and business continuity planning, and manage security threats.
Make smart technology choices: Assess new software, integrations and vendors for security risks.
Cut the admin: Automate onboarding, offboarding and device management alongside our People team.
Build security confidence: Support customer security questionnaires and run practical security awareness sessions for our global crew.

🙌 Qualifications And Fit

You know your way around a Mac-first environment and can explain security without making everyone’s eyes glaze over.

You will bring:

A relevant qualification in IT, Computer Science or Cyber Security, or equivalent professional experience.
Hands-on Jamf Pro experience, including smart groups, policies, configuration profiles, Self Service and Automated Device Enrollment.
Strong macOS knowledge, including FileVault key escrow, account recovery and device lockout troubleshooting.
Scripting skills in zsh, bash or Python to automate workflows.
Experience administering Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 and endpoint security tools such as CrowdStrike Falcon.
Practical SOC 2 or ISO 27001 experience, ideally with a compliance platform such as Drata.
A service-focused mindset, clear communication and the ability to prioritise when things get busy.

A few handy extras:
Relevant security certifications, AWS security expertise, or experience in a scaling SaaS company or the resources sector.

💎 Our Culture

Our best crew members are excited about building a great company. We take ownership, ask questions, share feedback and back each other.

Here is what forms part of our DNA:

First Principles Thinking: We believe in breaking down and understanding problems into their most basic parts. When we eat elephants, we do it one bite at a time.
LFG: We set high goals and ruthlessly prioritise to hit them. We push ourselves to act from first principles, speak up as we care about each other as humans and embrace feedback to win as a team.
Infectious Passion: We highly value team members who love the career path they’ve chosen and strive for mastery. We embrace the excitement of overcoming challenges, and growth. If you are driven and love what you do, you’ll thrive here,
Yes: We’re firm believers that we ‘can do’ until someone shows us the ‘can’t’. It’s funny how often the really gnarly problems are busted by folks who had no clue they were supposed to be unsolvable.
Create, Launch, and Evolve: Creation is the spark of learning. Launch it internally, engage with customers, gather feedback, and evolve. We focus on inputs - what we can control - which ultimately drives outcomes.

🚀 How to Apply

Ready to roll up your sleeves and join the CorePlan crew? Apply with your CV and cover letter letting us know what you can bring to the ream.

Questions? Drop us a line at careers@coreplan.io

Recruitment agencies: We appreciate your hustle, but we are managing this role directly. To get on our radar for future opportunities, email careers@coreplan.io

jobs.title: Engineering Project Manager
jobs.description:
At E Tech Group, joining our team means joining a group of passionate and forward-thinking experts. We’re one of the largest engineering and system integration firms in the United States providing value for our clients through IT automation and control solutions for more than 30 years to the Life Sciences, Mission Critical, Metals & Mining, Warehousing & Distribution, and CPG/Food & Beverage industries. Our national and global scale allows us to help our clients develop and implement standardized solutions at any of their facilities regardless of physical location or the local resources available at that site.

We are seeking a Project Manager
to lead a large project or multiple project efforts, which may include subcontractors, high dollar value material content and multiple resources within the Mission Critical Industry. Your responsibilities will include the management and coordination of the design, procurement, implementation, and commissioning phases of projects, including the commercial, financial, and technical success of projects ranging from $50K to $3.0M+.

You will take a leadership role in developing project proposals and vetting project cost estimates. You will develop and communicate a clear understanding of the client’s project goals and maintain the company’s alignment to these goals, enabling your team to exceed client expectations and budgeted profitability.

As a Project Manager, You Will:

Lead Proposal Development – Participate in proposal scope, schedule, and cost estimates, as well as Project Management methodology and project pricing and structure. Prepare for a successful handoff from Business Development.
Manage Client Communication – Ensure effective communication between the client, the project team, Business Development, and the management team at all phases of the project. Be effective at resolving scope, schedule and cost issues as they arise.
Project Schedule and Plan – Develop the project labor resource plan and procurement plan to meet the client’s schedule objective and project cash flow requirements.
Drive Scope – Maintain firm control of scope and compliance with specifications and contract requirements. Ensure that scope is well defined and communicated, and proactively obtain any required Change Orders, develop additional scope opportunities which may serve the client’s objective.
Maintain Cost – Develop and maintain project cost budgets and reports; manage estimated cost at completion, earned value, and contingency. Forecast monthly project costs avoiding cost overruns.
Lead the Project Team – Lead the project team in achieving the project tasks and milestones on schedule and under budget. Work closely with the Operations group to ensure that the right resources are assigned to the project at the optimal time. Communicate project progress to the team and to the client and be an effective advocate for the project team. Identify project risks in advance and mobilize the necessary resources to mitigate risks.
Present regular project activity and financial updates on projects to large audiences of customers and/or internal associates/management/Executives.
Become proficient in the extensive use of the E TECH GROUP PMO Methods, Tools and Process specific to project management standards.
Participate in the implementation of new project management tools that will be utilized across the enterprise.
Develop a strong level of understanding of E TECH GROUP’s Project Management Life (PMLC) Cycle Stages.
Be an ambassador who embodies our Core Values, prioritizing the success of E Tech Group, our clients, and the professional development of our associates.

You Have:

BS Engineering degree or equivalent education/experience background.
At least 3 years of dedicated project management experience or 5+ years in a project engineering environment.
Proficient in the utilization of project management principles, methods, and tools.
Ability to implement Project Management Institute (PMI) based standards into the E TECH GROUP culture, and serve as a mentor to other associates.
Proven project leadership on difficult projects, applications, solutions, and situations.
Proven performance in a stressful environment.
Excellent oral and written communication and presentation skills.
The ability to utilize technology to lead geographically dispersed project teams.
Experience managing contracts and/or subcontractors.
Experienced in the use of project management software such as MS Project.
Familiarity with industrial controls projects.
Experience with project budget / fiscal accountability.
A DNA comprised of collaboration and teamwork.

You May Have:

Controls Engineering background.
Experience with true design projects (EOR).
PMP Certified preferred
Experience managing control system, HMI, plant data historian, and other industrial projects

Benefits & Perks:

401k + match + prompt enrollment.  E Tech Group employees are 100% vested upon entry.
Prompt enrollment into Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits.
Generous paid time off that includes paid vacation, paid holidays, paid family leave and sick time off.
Learning and growth are key parts of the E Tech culture. We provide you with training and continuing education from day one, so you can advance your career. As an E Tech associate, you can unlock your greatest potential through challenges and opportunities.

E Tech Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, disability, military status, genetic information, gender identity, sexual orientation, citizenship status, or any other basis prohibited by law. E Tech Group will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and for religious beliefs. E Tech Group is an Affirmative Action Employer of individuals with disabilities and protected veterans.

Job Description

Do you want to be at the forefront of combating crypto-enabled terrorism financing? Are you excited about leading the intelligence research that helps financial institutions and governments disrupt illicit financial networks? Are you looking for a values-led company that trusts you to own your domain and make a real impact?

The Impact You Will Have

As a key contributor to our global intelligence team, you will act as a CTF Subject Matter Expert, leading complex, in-depth investigations into the use of cryptoassets by terrorist actors and facilitation networks. You will validate exposure and attribution confidence, improve workflows, and translate findings into actionable intelligence outputs.

Your work will directly enhance Elliptic’s industry-leading intelligence dataset and product capabilities, helping our private and public-sector customers and partners strengthen CTF controls, manage risk, and take defensible decisions. Your insights will inform strategic client conversations, shape impactful research and publications, and reinforce Elliptic’s reputation as a trusted authority in the crypto and financial intelligence space. Your expertise will play a vital role in advancing financial integrity on a truly global scale.

jobs.description:
How to Apply

A cover letter is required for consideration for this position and should be attached as the first page of your resume. The cover letter should address your specific interest in the position and outline how your skills and experience relate to the responsibilities and qualifications of this role.

Who We Are

The Division of Public Safety and Security conducts all police and security operations at the university (Ann Arbor, Dearborn, Flint). It is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year. DPSS offers an integrated approach to safety and security, partnering across the university and helping everyone in the U-M community take charge of their safety.

Proactive engagement with our community to provide compassionate and professional service is a DPSS core value.

Job Summary

The University of Michigan Division of Public Safety and Security (DPSS) is seeking a Security Intelligence Analyst, focused on Behavioral Threat Assessment, to support the University's Behavioral Threat Assessment and Management (BTAM) program. Under the direction of the DPSS Intelligence Police Sergeant, you will serve as a member of the DPSS Intelligence team responsible for collecting, evaluating, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence to support behavioral threat assessment and the division's broader security objectives.

As the Security Intelligence & Behavioral Threat Assessment Investigative Analyst, you support multidisciplinary BTAM teams by collecting and analyzing behavioral information, assessing static and dynamic risk factors, identifying protective factors, and developing evidence-based intervention and risk management strategies. To support the implementation of evidence-based BTAM methodologies, you provide objective behavioral assessments to support prevention, early intervention, and coordinated case management.

This position emphasizes behavior-based risk identification rather than reliance solely on criminal conduct or mental health diagnoses. You will collaborate with public safety personnel, mental health professionals, Human Resources, Student Life, legal counsel, Michigan Medicine, and other campuses and community partners to promote early identification of concerning behaviors, reduce the risk of targeted violence, and enhance the safety and well-being of the University community.

Responsibilities*

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Predictive Analysis: Conduct behavioral threat analysis by collecting, organizing, and evaluating information from multiple sources to produce reliable, actionable intelligence. Analyze behavioral patterns associated with targeted violence; assess static and dynamic risk factors, protective factors, and resiliency; and determine levels of concern and urgency using structured professional judgment. Monitor escalation and de-escalation indicators, evaluate an individual's progression along the pathway to violence, and provide evidence-based risk assessments and intervention recommendations to support multidisciplinary threat management and violence prevention efforts.
Investigative Support: Assist Threat Assessment leadership by serving as an active member of the Threat Assessment Team (TAT), a multidisciplinary committee with members from various stakeholder offices across campus. This includes leading meetings and coordinating reports as needed. Support ongoing investigations of highly sensitive and urgent real-time threat concerns, including potential threats of and/or acts of violence by affiliated or unaffiliated individuals that may affect the university community.
Risk Mitigation: Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies to reduce the risk of violence.
Prepare Intelligence Products: Prepare reports, bulletins, and threat assessments that articulate complex security concepts to inform and enhance campus safety measures.
Liaison : Serve as liaison between DPSS departments and other internal and external partners, including local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, to ensure the timely sharing of critical information and foster collaboration. Conduct educational and outreach efforts on critical topics related to Threat Assessment (e.g., behaviors of concern, de-escalation techniques, reporting process) through in-person and virtual presentations, social media, traditional marketing materials, and other multimedia efforts.
BTAM Program Support : Serve as the Intelligence team's primary analytical resource assigned to support the University's BTAM program. Work closely with the Director of Behavioral Threat Assessment and multidisciplinary threat assessment teams on BTAM case assignments, case prioritization, structured assessment methodologies, and intervention strategies, while maintaining alignment with DPSS Intelligence policies, analytical standards, information-handling requirements, and operating protocols.
Confidential Support: Perform independent and confidential tasks related to strategic intelligence, maintaining the highest level of discretion in handling sensitive information.

Required Qualifications*

Bachelor's degree in Criminal Justice, Public Safety, Criminal Analysis, Homeland Security, or a related field, or equivalent education and experience.
A minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in behavioral threat assessment, criminal investigations, intelligence analysis, law enforcement, public safety, corporate security, emergency management, behavioral health, case management, or a related field, focusing on intelligence operations or analysis.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
Experience with computer software related to intelligence analysis applications and online social media, chat, dark web, and open-source sites.
Familiarity with principles and practices of threat management and assessment to identify, monitor, and report potential online threats and heightened activity.
Experience with principles and practices of crime and data analysis, analytical research methods, and criminal intelligence related to researching, collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data.
Experience conducting behavioral, investigative, or intelligence analysis involving complex or sensitive cases.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated effectiveness in complex, decentralized organizations.
Ability to adapt work hours to accommodate various University events and initiatives.
Prior experience in a confidential, high-demand environment.
Proficiency with MS Office, Google Drive, and related software.
Valid driver's license with a driving record of fewer than 6 points.
Must pass a comprehensive public safety background investigation, psychological exam, and physical and drug screening.

Modes of Work

Positions that are eligible for hybrid or mobile/remote work mode are at the discretion of the hiring department. Work agreements are reviewed annually at a minimum and are subject to change at any time, and for any reason, throughout the course of employment. Learn more about the work modes.

Additional Information

All members of DPSS are considered Campus Security Authorities (CSAs) under the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act. As such, you are required to report any Clery reportable offenses that come to your attention. DPSS employees must also complete the Clery Compliance training within 14 days of employment and annually thereafter.

Application Deadline

Job openings are posted for a minimum of seven calendar days. This job may be removed from posting boards and filled anytime after the minimum posting period has ended.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst, Lumina Data Platform
jobs.description:
Overview

We are building a cloud-native data platform that ingests, governs, and serves data to teams across the company. We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst who can turn that data into clear, trustworthy answers — and document it well enough that others can reuse the work. You will sit close to the platform and its consumers, analyzing data to drive decisions while writing the queries, definitions, and guides that make the platform easier for everyone to use.

This role blends deep analytical work with strong technical writing. You will not only produce analysis, you will document data sources, metrics, and how-to guidance so that self-service actually works. We move fast and use AI as a normal part of the job, so we want someone who reaches for those tools to raise the quality and speed of their work.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

Deliver analysis that drives decisions — scope questions with stakeholders, pull and model data from the platform, and turn it into clear findings and recommendations.
Be the go-to expert on the platform's data — develop deep knowledge of the data model, the data it holds, and the platform's capabilities, and answer questions from consumers about what data exists, what it means, and how to use it.
Own metrics and definitions — define, validate, and maintain the key metrics teams rely on, and keep them consistent across the platform.
Write technical documentation — document data sources, schemas, metric definitions, and query patterns so consumers can find and trust the data without a meeting.
Enable self-service — build reusable queries, dashboards, and how-to guides that let other teams answer their own questions.
Safeguard data quality — profile new and existing sources, flag anomalies, and partner with data engineering to resolve issues at the source.
Be a bridge to the platform — translate consumer needs into feedback for the platform team, and help onboard teams onto new data as it lands.
Work AI-forward — use AI tools as a default part of how you analyze, draft SQL, summarize findings, and produce documentation — and share what works with the team.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

5+ years in data analysis, business intelligence, or a similar role delivering analysis that shaped real decisions.
Strong SQL — you can independently query, join, and model data in a cloud warehouse; comfort with a scripting language such as Python is a plus.
Data platform fluency — hands-on understanding of modern cloud data architectures, data pipelines, and schemas; able to trace data from source to consumption, identify data issues, and partner effectively on technical solutions.
Technical writing skills — you write clear, well-organized documentation — data dictionaries, metric definitions, runbooks, and how-to guides — that non-experts can follow.
Rigor and clarity — you validate your numbers, explain your assumptions, and communicate findings simply to technical and non-technical audiences.
AI-forward mindset — you actively use AI tools to do your best work and raise your leverage, and you stay current as the tooling evolves.
US-based — authorized to work in the United States; this role is open to US-based candidates.

Nice to Have

Real estate / proptech experience — familiarity with property, leasing, or real estate data is desired but not required.
Experience standing up or maintaining a data catalog, data dictionary, or metrics layer.
Experience supporting internal consumers of a shared data platform.
Familiarity with dbt, version control, or documentation-as-code workflows.

How We'll Measure Success

Analysis that stakeholders act on, delivered accurately and on time.
A well-documented, trusted set of metrics and data sources that others reuse.
Growth in self-service — teams answering their own questions from your guides and queries.
Faster, higher-quality output through effective use of AI tools.

Salary And Benefits

RealPage provides a competitive salary package along with a comprehensive benefit plan that includes:

Health, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement savings plan with company match.
Paid time off and holidays.
Professional development opportunities.
Performance-based bonus based on position.

Compensation may vary depending on your location, qualifications including job-related education, training, experience, licensure, and certification, that could result at a level outside of these ranges. Certain roles are eligible for additional rewards, including annual bonus, and sales incentives depending on the terms of the applicable plan and role as well as individual performance.

Equal Opportunity Employer: RealPage Company is an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Pay Range

USD $85,200.00 - USD $145,200.00 /Yr.

Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

About the role

We're hiring a Senior Audit Program Manager, Security Assurance to lead security audits and certification programs as Nscale scales its global AI infrastructure. This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Director, Security Risk & Compliance. You'll lead assigned SOC 2 and ISO 27001 engagements across cloud services, data centers, and corporate functions, from scoping and readiness through external assessment, remediation, and final reporting.

You'll join our existing Audit and Assurance team, sharing a growing portfolio of audits, certification activities, and scope expansions. You'll own your assigned engagements and workstreams while maintaining a consistent approach to controls, evidence, and auditor engagement across the portfolio.

We're looking for an experienced assurance practitioner who can work directly with engineers, understand how controls operate, and substantiate those controls to external auditors. You'll investigate gaps, bring sound judgment to ambiguous requirements, and recommend practical solutions. You'll also help us scale assurance through reusable evidence, automation, and well-designed workflows.

What you'll be doing

Audit and Certification Delivery

Lead assigned SOC 2 and ISO 27001 engagements, including readiness assessments, scope expansions, ongoing assessments, and remediation.
Establish audit plans with clear boundaries, control owners, evidence requirements, milestones, and dependencies. Coordinate observation periods, fieldwork, and report or certificate delivery with external auditors.
Serve as the primary auditor contact for your engagements. Lead control walkthroughs, prepare technical teams for interviews, and resolve evidence requests and interpretation questions.

Audit Coordination and Reporting

Manage audit requests, schedules, and status reviews across concurrent engagements. Assign owners, set deadlines, review submissions, document decisions, and drive follow-through on blockers and recovery plans.
Prepare audit documentation, including application letters, scoping questionnaires, evidence request lists, and management responses. Review draft reports and certification documents for factual accuracy, scope, and consistency with evidence, and coordinate approvals and signatures.
Maintain an organized, version-controlled record of evidence, correspondence, approvals, and final deliverables. Surface delivery risks early with practical recommendations.

Technical Controls and Evidence Quality

Assess control design and operating effectiveness with engineering, security, IT, and business owners. Translate assessment criteria into clear implementation and evidence requirements.
Review technical evidence across identity and access management, GPU/compute infrastructure configuration, change management, logging, vulnerability management, backup and recovery, and physical security.
Validate evidence before submission, including its source, completeness, relevant population, period, and connection to the control being tested.
Investigate discrepancies between documented controls and actual operations. Work with owners to correct the control, documentation, or evidence, and maintain accurate control narratives, framework mappings, and relevant Statement of Applicability inputs.

Scope Expansion and Shared Responsibilities

Assess how new services, sites, entities, and operating models affect audit boundaries and certification coverage. Establish readiness criteria for scope expansion and make coverage gaps and their business implications clear.
Work with cloud, infrastructure, data center, and colocation teams to distinguish Nscale-operated controls from provider responsibilities and inherited controls.
Evaluate provider reports and certificates for relevant services, locations, periods, exceptions, and customer responsibilities. Identify where additional evidence or assessment is needed.
Partner with Customer Trust and Legal to translate validated customer obligations into assurance requirements, and with the SRC TPM to connect them to delivery dependencies.

Findings and Continuous Assurance

Turn audit findings and readiness gaps into remediation plans with accountable owners, root causes, due dates, and closure criteria.
Challenge incomplete fixes, verify remediation evidence, and coordinate retesting and auditor acceptance where required.
Track overdue actions, recurring control failures, and changes that could affect upcoming assessments. Support ISMS reviews and internal assurance activities with accurate audit results, control performance, and improvement recommendations.

Automation and Program Improvement

Partner with Compliance Automation to define evidence requirements, identify reliable source systems, and validate automated collection and monitoring outputs.
Build reusable evidence and control mappings that reduce repeated requests while preserving each assessment's scope and period requirements.
Improve audit workflows in Drata and connected delivery tools so owners, evidence, findings, and decisions remain traceable.
Use AI tools to streamline repeatable assurance work, with appropriate data handling and verification of generated outputs.

KPIs

Audit and certification milestone delivery against agreed plans
Evidence submission readiness, avoidable rework, auditor-query resolution time, and accuracy and completeness of scope records, control ownership, and evidence mappings
Remediation closure against agreed criteria, overdue findings, and recurring issues
Reduction in duplicated evidence requests and manual effort against a defined baseline

About You

Required

7+ years of experience in security assurance, technology audit, compliance, or related disciplines, including independently leading external audit or certification engagements in technical environments.
Substantial hands-on experience with both SOC 2 and ISO 27001, with accountability for delivering audits or assessments through final reports or certification outcomes.
Experience working directly with external auditors, leading walkthroughs, resolving control and evidence questions, and managing findings through verified closure.
Technical fluency in cloud infrastructure and security controls. You can discuss how a control is implemented with engineers and assess whether the evidence supports its claimed design and operation.
Experience defining assessment scope and understanding shared responsibilities across internal teams, cloud providers, and other service providers.
Strong program execution across concurrent engagements, including dependency management, prioritization, and timely escalation with practical recommendations.
Ability to investigate unfamiliar issues independently, distinguish facts from assumptions, and communicate a clear recommendation with supporting evidence.
Clear written communication, including control narratives, remediation requirements, and concise leadership reporting.

Strong Preferences

Security assurance experience at a cloud service provider, hyperscaler, infrastructure platform, or data center operator.
Experience expanding audit or certification scope across multiple services, sites, or entities.
Experience with common control frameworks, evidence reuse, continuous monitoring, and reducing the effort audits require from engineering teams.
Strong familiarity with AI tools to automate repeatable processes and streamline workflows, with practical examples of improvements to quality or efficiency.
Hands-on experience with Drata or a comparable GRC platform, including control mapping, evidence workflows, and findings management.
Experience building effective assurance processes in a fast-growing organization with evolving systems and ownership.

Nice to Have

Prior experience as an external technology auditor or ISO 27001 auditor.
CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, or equivalent practical expertise.
Ability to use SQL, scripting, or APIs to inspect evidence and improve reporting.
Experience with GPU infrastructure, Kubernetes, or infrastructure as code.

What we can offer you

At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.

Highly competitive US compensation package (base + bonus + equity), with performance reviews every 12 months. 🚀
Join one of the fastest-growing AI infrastructure companies — your chance to directly shape how global AI capacity is planned and deployed. ✨
Expect a dynamic progression plan tailored to your ambitions. Grow by leading critical cross-functional initiatives and shaping capital strategy — always with our full support.
Human-First Flexibility: We treat you as humans first. 🫶🏽 Our flexible workplace trusts Nscalers to deliver, giving you the autonomy to shape your day around life's moments.

📍 Brussels | Full-time | Hybrid

The energy sector is changing fast. New technologies, new market mechanisms and an increasingly complex energy system are reshaping the way electricity markets operate.

For a major player in the Belgian energy sector
, we're looking for a Business Analyst – Energy
who wants to work at the heart of these developments.

This is not your typical IT Business Analyst role. You'll combine data analysis, market operations, problem-solving and stakeholder collaboration
while building valuable expertise in the Belgian energy market.

We're primarily looking for someone who's analytically strong, curious and eager to understand how complex systems work.

🚀 What you'll be working on

You'll contribute to the operation and further development of an important mechanism within the Belgian electricity market, helping ensure that our energy system remains reliable and future-proof.

Your role will be varied. You'll:
📊 Analyse technical, financial and operational data
and translate your findings into clear recommendations.
⚡ Help run and monitor key energy-market processes
, from participant qualification and market operations to performance monitoring and settlement.
🔎 Dive into complex or exceptional cases and work with different experts to find the right solution.
📈 Monitor KPIs, calculations and market results
and contribute to internal and external reporting.
🤝 Work with internal experts and external market participants to answer questions and solve operational challenges.
💡 Look for opportunities to make processes simpler, smarter and more efficient
through digitalisation, automation and continuous improvement.
🧪 Test new functionalities and help ensure that new solutions work in practice.
🎯 Gradually become a go-to expert in your domain
, taking on more responsibility as your knowledge grows.

You'll be supported by experienced colleagues, so you're not expected to master the complexity of the energy market from day one. The role is explicitly designed to allow someone to build deeper subject-matter expertise over time.

We're deliberately keeping the profile broad.

You might currently be working as a Business Analyst, Operations Analyst, Energy Analyst, Consultant, Process Analyst
or in another analytical role.

You'll probably feel at home in this position if you:
🎓 Have a Master's degree in Engineering, Economics, Business, Finance, Data Analytics or a related field.
💼 Have around 2–5 years of relevant professional experience
in analysis, operations, consulting, process management, financial operations or a similar environment.
🧠 Enjoy working with data, numbers and complex problems
.

Experience in energy is a plus, not a must.
Experience with Python or other data-analysis tools is also a nice-to-have rather than a requirement.

while working on topics that have a tangible impact on how our future energy system operates.

You'll gain exposure to energy markets, data, financial processes, regulation, digitalisation and a broad range of stakeholders

And as your expertise grows, so will your responsibility.

Salesforce Certified Administrator (required).

Clear writer who can explain what changed and why to non-technical teammates.
